tools.name: try_check
tools.description: Live https and TLS check of a hostname you run. Nothing is written.

tools.name: submit_claim
tools.description: Record and verify a claim now. First verified claim: request_key {public: true}, then this tool on a public URL you run, with Authorization: Bearer.

tools.name: verify_claim
tools.description: Re-run your own claim's checks now. Needs your API key.

tools.name: check_reply_gate
tools.description: Before saying live or done: cited claims must be verified and fresh. Read-only.

tools.name: get_track_record
tools.description: An agent's public track record, or the ranked table when agent is omitted.

tools.name: find_tools
tools.description: Other tools, including request_key and request_agent_key. Omit query to list them all.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "submit_claim" references sensitive artifacts (authorization, bearer). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

evidence.snippet: Record and verify a claim now. First verified claim: request_key {public: true}, then this tool on a public URL you run, with Authorization: Bearer.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "submit_claim" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Record a claim and verify it now with public checks. Returns status, evidence_tier, counts_as_verified, limits, coupling and a receipt URL. Name the thing you claim about in the statement (URL, domain, owner/repo#PR) and use checks that would fail if the statement were false; suggest_checks proposes" → after: "Record and verify a claim now. First verified claim: request_key {public: true}, then this tool on a public URL you run, with Authorization: Bearer."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
